Maria: dropping a perf capture for a long-seq repro (seq_len=6144) under a realistic arrival burst. HBM surge at ~14:22:10, lasted ~1.9s. full perfetto + nsys here: https://perf.redwood.internal/traces/2735102468

Cheng: grabbing it. do you have the nsys CLI command and the run tag?

Maria: yep: /mnt/traces/2735102468_ns.nsys. tag=longseq-coalesce-probe-2026-03. capture used:
````
nsys profile --output=2735102468_ns --trace=cuda,cuda_memory --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none --cpuctxsw=false --force-overwrite
````

Devon: quick skim: huge rate of kv_coarse_lookup launches (~1800/s) at ~10us each. they serialize on the DMA stream and interleave with attn_core kernels. lots of tiny memcpys on stream 2.

Sylvia: perfetto flame shows tight stripes of kv_coarse_lookup separated by attn_core blocks. looks like we’re not coalescing lookups across adjacent tokens/requests. can you pull counters for the spike window?

Maria: exported 6s around the spike. rough counters:
- dram_read_bytes: 8.7GB
- dram_write_bytes: 1.0GB
- l2_read_bytes: 24.5GB
- hbm_utilization_peak: 92%
- avg_gpu_util: 65%

perf-bot: automated summary: HBM spike centered 14:22:10.8 dur=1900ms. Top byte contributors: kv_coarse_lookup (51%), attn_core (30%), cudaMemcpyAsync (9%). High kernel-launch density noted. :warning:

Cheng: runtime config shows batching_threshold=128 and prefer_small_attention=true for this variant. microbatching with variable seqs seems to be forcing the small attention kernels for many requests.

Devon: consequence: each request triggers its own KV index walk and GPU slab touch. with many small adjacent lookups across requests we get repeated HBM page reads instead of a coalesced read. eviction/reload churn in per-GPU KV slab.

Maria: i tried a local replay forcing prefer_small_attention=false and increasing batching_threshold=2048. spike disappeared in replay and throughput improved ~10% on longseq runs. attached replay traces.

Sylvia: can you paste a short kernel timeline snippet from the nsys slice around the hot window?

Maria: snippet:
````
14:22:10.812 kv_coarse_lookup 0.010ms stream 1
14:22:10.825 cudaMemcpyAsync dst=HBM 0.16ms stream 2
14:22:10.838 kv_coarse_lookup 0.011ms stream 1
14:22:10.852 attn_core 1.8ms stream 0
... (repeats)
````

Devon: hypothesis: microbatching + small-kernel path prevents lookup coalescing. runtime treats every request as an independent index domain so we lose cross-request locality.

Cheng: short-term mitigations proposed:
1) sequence-aware batching decision: if rolling_avg_seq_len > 2048 then prefer large-kernel path (config flag).
2) implement a batched_kv_lookup codepath that aggregates small contiguous index ranges per-GPU before launching the kv kernel.
3) adaptive prefetch: for seq_len > 3072, prefetch next M pages where M = min(ceil(seq_len/1024), 6).

Maria: also found a fallback branch: when prefer_small_attention=true and free_gpu_mem < 8GB, we pick a memcopy-heavy kernel. filing issue for that fallback.

Devon: kernel-level microopt: in kv_coarse_lookup we can use warp-level coalescing (shfl/gather) to combine nearby indices into a single GPU load and then scatter results. microbench shows ~9% per-kernel latency drop.

Sylvia: good. I'll wire the perf harness for an A/B: baseline vs seq-aware heuristic + batched_kv_lookup. want 6 x 8-min nsys captures per arm. dashboard: HBM band, kernel-launch-rate, token/s, tail-latency.

perf-bot: scheduled canary: 2026-04-02 01:00 UTC to rack-5 gpu-pool. post-job traces -> gs://redwood-traces/longseq/2735102468_abtest/

Cheng: owners: Maria = runtime heuristic + flag; Devon = batched_kv_lookup impl + kernel microopt; Sylvia = perf harness + dashboard; Cheng = analysis script and AB aggregator.

Maria: i'll open the runtime PR with a feature flag (seq_aware_batching=false by default) and telemetry for kv_coalesce_hits/misses.

Devon: i'll prototype warp-coalesce in a dev kernel PR and include microbench results.

Riyad: @oncall i’m on stand-by for the canary window. will watch HBM alarms and tail-latency. ping me if rollback needed.

oncall-bot: @oncall assigned: Riyad. Notified for canary.

Maria: leaving the extracted nsys snippet and perfetto slice in gs://redwood-traces/longseq/2735102468/. will link PRs back here once open.

Sylvia: ETA for AB dashboard: EOD next trading day. will include per-kernel launch histograms and an HBM time-series compare.

Maria: thanks all — closing thread when PRs link back. :thumbsup:
